title: Explode / How it’s made
note: Educational assembly order · H-10 internals approximate · Not a factory assembly guide

closing.title: A movement becomes a watch.
closing.description: Stored energy, a steady rhythm, a readable display and a protective case. Every layer now has a place—and a reason to be here.

chapters.title: Start with the movement.
chapters.description: The H-10 movement gives the watch its rhythm. A mainspring stores energy, gears transmit it, and the escapement and balance regulate its release. Explore this small mechanism before building the watch around it.
chapters.joined: The movement is the foundation. Next, connect it to the motion of your wrist.

chapters.title: Let your wrist supply the energy.
chapters.description: The weighted rotor swings around its bearing as the watch moves. Beneath it, the winding train replenishes the mainspring. Its openings let you glimpse the mechanism it serves.
chapters.joined: The automatic movement is together. Turn toward the side that will tell the time.

chapters.title: Turn motion into something readable.
chapters.description: The matte dial gives time a fixed scale: hour numerals and fine minute divisions. It stays still while the hands move above it.
chapters.joined: The scale is in place. Add the pointers that make it useful.

chapters.title: Give time its pointers.
chapters.description: Three hands share a center at different heights. The cathedral outlines frame luminous inserts; the hour, minute and seconds hands make different timescales visible.
chapters.joined: The mechanism now has a readable face. It still needs protection.

chapters.title: Build a home around it.
chapters.description: The steel case surrounds the movement and display. Its openings and supports connect the internal assembly to the crown, windows and strap.
chapters.joined: The case brings the layers into one object. Now connect the controls.

chapters.title: Put control within reach.
chapters.description: The crown provides the wearer’s connection to setting and winding. Its gripped edge makes a small mechanical control usable by hand.
chapters.joined: The control joins the case. Next, attend to its boundaries.

chapters.title: Pay attention to the joins.
chapters.description: Gaskets belong at interfaces between case parts. Their placement matters as much as the visible metal; this illustrative model does not establish actual sealing performance.
chapters.joined: The interfaces are represented. Close the back while keeping the mechanism visible.

chapters.title: Frame a view from behind.
chapters.description: The metal caseback ring retains the rear window and closes around the movement. The back is an assembly with its own structure, not a painted surface.
chapters.joined: The retaining ring is in place. Its opening still needs a window.

chapters.title: Keep the mechanism in view.
chapters.description: The transparent rear window lets you see the rotor beneath it. Its material composition is unverified in our references, so we do not label it sapphire.
chapters.joined: The rear is closed and still transparent. Protect the display on the other side.

chapters.title: Protect the face without hiding it.
chapters.description: The front sapphire sits above the hands. Its curved edge and moving reflections reveal a clear protective surface while preserving the view of the dial.
chapters.joined: The display is protected. One last connection makes the watch wearable.

chapters.title: Bring it back to the wrist.
chapters.description: The leather strap connects the case to the wearer. That closes the story: the wrist carries the watch, and its motion helps wind the mechanism inside.
chapters.joined: The layers have become one watch. Scroll a little farther to see it together.

opening.title: A whole world on your wrist.
opening.description: Start with the complete Murph. Scroll into its movement, then follow each layer back into place to discover how the watch works.
